reason: This passage (Exodus 32:25-29) describes an internal religious conflict within the Hebrew people themselves. The conflict centers on idolatry and apostasy—the worship of the Golden Calf—and God's response through Moses. The conflict is explicitly religious in nature, not national, and involves the Levites punishing fellow Hebrews for violating the covenant. Notably, no Egyptians are mentioned or depicted in this passage at all. The text depicts conflict as fundamentally about religious faithfulness (loyalty to God) versus religious transgression (idol worship), not as a national conflict between Hebrew and Egyptian peoples.
